about: References for the related-work section bankperm/RELATED_WORK_EN.md. Field n is the [n] used there (null if not cited there); field paper_n is the [n] of bankperm/PAPER_EN.md (null if not cited there; the paper cites the 9 references with a paper_n (2026-10-20; roofline was dropped), so the other entries are kept here but not cited in it). The two numberings differ. Each entry was checked on 2026-10-18 against Crossref, the arXiv API, NeurIPS proceedings metadata or the patent page; 'verified' says what was read. 'balances' is what the cited work equalizes; 'preempts_claim' is judged against the claim stated in RELATED_WORK_EN.md (Novelty position). Notes here that call the tap skew unevaluated or a baseline still to add (top-level claim, budnik_kuck, last novelty threat) predate 2928d28: PAPER_EN.md now counts the skew on the board network after the study (not run on the board).
claim: Offline, function-preserving channel-to-bank permutation, chosen on calibration activations to minimise the per-window maximum bank nonzero count of a lockstep-bank zero-skipping integer CNN core (P=16, T=4, XC7Z020), folded into the producer's filters, bias and requantisation and the consumer's weights; RTL, bitstream and integer output unchanged; given the (ky, kx, channel) window order. On this platform the host builds the windows, so tap-level layouts (any static order of a window's taps, with the weight columns) are also exact; they are not evaluated.

references.title: Cnvlutin: Ineffectual-neuron-free deep neural network computing
references.venue: Proc. ACM/IEEE 43rd Annual Int. Symp. Computer Architecture (ISCA)
references.verified: Crossref metadata; full text read (Sec. IV-B2 window split into 16 slices, weights rearranged statically in software; Sec. IV-B5 lanes idle until all lanes finish the window)
references.what_it_does: Skips zero activations; each window's input channels are split into 16 slices, one per neuron lane; all lanes move to the next window together.
references.balances: none; it measures the resulting lane-synchronization stall as its own category
references.static_or_dynamic: static slice assignment, dynamic zero skipping
references.hardware_changes: new ASIC lanes, offset encoding, per-lane fetch
references.how_this_work_differs: Same max-over-lanes cost as our banks; we change which channels share a lane (bank) to shrink that stall, without changing the hardware.
references.preempts_claim: no; it defines the problem the permutation addresses

references.title: SCNN: An accelerator for compressed-sparse convolutional neural networks
references.venue: Proc. 44th Annu. Int. Symp. Computer Architecture (ISCA)
references.verified: Crossref metadata; full text read (fraction of cycles waiting at inter-PE barriers due to load imbalance)
references.what_it_does: Cartesian-product dataflow over compressed nonzero weights and activations.
references.balances: none; reports idle time at inter-PE barriers
references.hardware_changes: new ASIC dataflow and accumulator array
references.how_this_work_differs: Two-sided ASIC design; we keep a one-sided activation-skipping FPGA core fixed and relabel channels offline.

references.title: SparTen: A sparse tensor accelerator for convolutional neural networks
references.venue: Proc. 52nd Annu. IEEE/ACM Int. Symp. Microarchitecture (MICRO)
references.verified: Crossref metadata; abstract (OpenAlex); full text of the SparTen chapter (Ch. 3) of A. Gondimalla's Purdue PhD dissertation (Dec. 2022, figshare 21673115), Sec. 3.3.3: GB-S 'simply sorts all the filters of a layer by whole-filter density' and statically 'unshuffles' the next layer's weights; implicit barrier at each input-map broadcast within a cluster. The MICRO'19 PDF itself was not read (ACM 403).
references.what_it_does: Two-sided sparse inner-join accelerator; greedy balancing GB-S sorts whole filters by density offline and statically reorders ('unshuffles') the next layer's weights to match; GB-H groups at finer granularity, pairs dense and sparse filters on one compute unit and needs a permutation network. It traces load imbalance to broadcast reuse of input maps across filters of different density.
references.static_or_dynamic: GB-S static (offline); GB-H hybrid with run-time permutation network
references.function_preserving: yes (output-channel permutation compensated in the next layer)
references.hardware_changes: new accelerator; GB-H needs a permutation network
references.how_this_work_differs: Closest folding precedent: same offline relabel-and-compensate mechanism, but the objective is weight density, not per-window activation nonzeros across lockstep banks.
references.preempts_claim: partially: the fold-into-next-layer mechanism and offline greedy balancing (not the activation objective)

references.how_this_work_differs: Weight-side sparsity; our core skips activation zeros and stays unchanged.

references.title: S2TA: Exploiting structured sparsity for energy-efficient mobile CNN acceleration

references.title: Sense: Model-hardware codesign for accelerating sparse CNNs on systolic arrays
references.venue: IEEE Trans. Very Large Scale Integr. (VLSI) Syst.
references.verified: Crossref metadata; arXiv full text (Sec. III-B: 'Since IFMs are generated dynamically, they cannot be trained offline to balance IFM workload'; Sec. IV-D channel clustering module)

references.function_preserving: activation clustering yes; weight pruning no
references.how_this_work_differs: Closest activation-balancing FPGA work; ours is static, uses per-window co-activation instead of per-channel density, and adds no hardware.

references.title: Crane: Mitigating accelerator under-utilization caused by sparsity irregularities in CNNs
references.venue: IEEE Trans. Comput.
references.verified: Crossref metadata; full text read ('Since activation sparsity is generated dynamically ... no workload balancing can be done offline'). references.how_this_work_differs: Ours balances activation work in expectation with no run-time hardware.

novelty_threats: SparTen GB-S [3]: offline density sort of whole filters with the next layer's weights reordered to match (the dense/sparse pairing is GB-H). Same mechanism (relabel output channels, compensate downstream, no hardware); differs only in using weight density. A reviewer can call our method 'GB-S with activation statistics'.

VARA [19]: offline co-zero affinity over sliding windows, greedy permutation of input dimensions, weights reordered offline. Same ingredients; opposite objective (cluster zeros) and a run-time index unit.
BRIM [10]: offline balancing from profiled activation statistics (by pruning, plus hardware). Removes 'offline activation-statistics balancing' as a novelty.
Pool and Yu [15], TETRIS [16]: channel permutation absorbed into neighbouring layers is standard.

Sense [11] states that input maps 'cannot be trained offline to balance IFM workload' (Crane [12] is said to state the same, but its full text could not be re-checked); our result contradicts them only in expectation, so the claim must say 'in expectation over held-out inputs', not 'balanced'.

S2TA [8] and the Moffett patent [9] already balance activation banks (by discarding activations), so 'bank balancing is not available for activation sparsity' is false; the contrast must be 'function-preserving'.

Tap-level layouts (review of 2026-10-18): because the host builds the windows, any static order of a window's taps with the weight columns is exact. An uncommitted count of a data-free skew (channel p at 3x3 position s to slot (p+s) mod N, each channel's taps 3/2/2/2 over the banks) saved more than both fitted channel relabelings on B-32 ReLU s1 (05.png 12,139,748 vs 12,355,274 Frozen and 12,277,883 Multi-start; 9.20% pooled over 79 images vs 7.46% and 8.10%), and on 8 images of B and maxout s1. With skewed storage [30] as precedent, the channel relabeling is not the best static layout on this platform; the paper must add this baseline or justify a fixed window order.

findings: Sec. 3 says Multi-Bank Hash Selection (Xu, Pu, Wang) itself reports that a crossbar between banks and compute units burdens logic and floorplan. Wrong: in Xu et al. Sec. 4.5 that sentence describes the compared work 'TCAS1'22' [33], whose reference entry is Xie, Lin, Wang, Wei, IEEE TCAS-I 68(7):2936-2949, 2021, doi 10.1109/TCSI.2021.3074300. Xu et al.'s own design uses a hash-selected multi-bank feature-map cache.
Sec. 4 builds the 'opposite-sign area result explained by the crossbar' argument on that misreading; if kept, it must be argued against Xie et al. (TCAS-I 2021), not Xu et al.
Sec. 3 dates the paper 2024. It is Micromachines vol. 16, no. 1, art. 22 (2025), first published online 27 Dec 2024; cite as 2025.

Sec. 3 says static load balancing is reported to be ineffective for dynamic activation sparsity, without a source. Correct sources: Crane (Guan et al., IEEE TC 69(7):931-943, 2020) and Sense (Sun et al., IEEE TVLSI 31(4):470-483, 2023). Xu et al. balance weight workload only and leave activation sparsity to future work.
